research_updates.title: Three Google taxpayer accounts remain separate
research_updates.notes: The 2024 city report identifies Gable Corp., Questa LLC and Tetra LLC as Google. Their rounded taxable values are dated January 1, 2022 even though the table calls them current-year 2024 data. They are recorded once as separate account stocks, not summed or presented as a trend. Parcel, campus and building allocation remains unresolved.

source.notes: Principal Area Taxpayers table is in the unaudited statistical section. research_updates.title: The 2022 Council Bluffs award remains in performance
research_updates.notes: IEDA continues to list contract 23-HQJPTC-005 as an under-contract performance-period project, with $600 million capital investment and 31 jobs contracted for completion by October 31, 2029. These remain commitments. The table's zero maximum state tax benefit does not establish a zero local property-tax exemption, and no realized investment, filled-job count, abatement value, payment, receipt, or taxpayer-account allocation is inferred.

source.title: IEDA 2025 Annual Report
source.notes: The projects-under-contract table retains Google LLC contract 23-HQJPTC-005 in Council Bluffs with $600 million of total project cost and capital investment, 31 contracted created jobs, a $28.73 qualifying wage, an October 31, 2029 completion date, and an October 31, 2031 maintenance date. The table reports zero direct funding and zero maximum state tax benefit while the project award is a local property-tax exemption; it does not quantify the exemption or establish realized investment, jobs, or local tax receipts. The report is dated January 31, 2026 and reports contract status as of June 30, 2025.

research_updates.title: Wider Iowa impact-model outputs remain contextual
research_updates.notes: The Deloitte study reports statewide direct, indirect, induced, and total GDP, jobs, and labor-income estimates for 2021-2023 using IMPLAN and Google-provided inputs. Those outputs are not inserted as observed Council Bluffs records or re-modeled here because they combine channels, years, and Iowa data-center activity without a selected-building allocation.

source.title: Google's Data Center Impact in Iowa — 2024 Impact Study
source.publisher: Google LLC and Deloitte Consulting LLP
source.notes: Deloitte prepared the study for Google using Google-provided, public, and third-party information without independent verification. The report identifies $285,000 invested during 2019-2023 in the Council Bluffs Community School District STEM and Computer Science Diploma Pathways program. Wider Iowa economic-impact outputs are IMPLAN-modeled and are not entered as observed project records.

research_updates.title: Assessor and treasurer audit resolved two principal operating parcels
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Pottawattamie County GIS parcel layer, County Treasurer parcel search, linked assessor cards, and tax histories. Queries: owner SQL OWNER LIKE '%QUESTA%' OR OWNER LIKE '%TETRA%' OR OWNER LIKE '%GOOGLE%', then parcel IDs 744333101001 and 744411476005. Date range reviewed: tax years 2018-2025 plus current parcel/deed fields. Positive results are recorded separately as parcel stocks, bills, and payments. Negative result: the current GIS query did not return a corporate Gable owner row; eight additional Tetra/Questa land parcels had no address or material building value, and no company-wide rollup, personal-property account, jurisdiction distribution, or paid 2025 ordinary-tax evidence was found.

source.title: Pottawattamie County GIS public parcel layer
source.notes: Owner query OWNER LIKE '%QUESTA%' OR OWNER LIKE '%TETRA%' OR OWNER LIKE '%GOOGLE%' returned ten records. It resolved the two addressed parcels used in the tax audit—Questa 744333101001 at 10410 Bunge Avenue and Tetra 744411476005 at 1430 Veterans Memorial Highway—plus eight mostly unaddressed land parcels. Values from the live tax-detail pages, which carry tax years, are used instead of undated GIS totals.

research_updates.title: Planning, permit, and contractor-record audit found valued work packages but no supplier payments
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Council Bluffs Archive Center, City Council and Planning Commission packets, Building Division monthly permit reports, and the public permit map service. Queries included Google, Gable, Questa, Tetra, 10410 Bunge, 1430 Veterans Memorial, SLN 4A/5A/6A, and data center across 2007-2025. Positive quantitative results are the two 2025 permit valuations. Other reports identify contractors including JE Dunn, Whiting-Turner, Michels Power, DNB Electric, Miller Electric, Mainelli Mechanical, and MMC, but no invoices, payments, vendor residence, payroll, local-purchase share, completion cost, or procurement award was found. Therefore supplier retention remains unmodeled.

research_updates.title: Development agreement required developer-funded sewer improvements without a disclosed value
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: 2009 development-agreement references, 2012 annexation planning minutes, 2013 sewer-dedication packet, and later agreement amendments. Record identifiers: January 16, 2009 development agreement and the 975-acre tract sewer-line, pump-station, and appurtenance dedication. The packet establishes developer responsibility, completion, City acceptance, and a two-year maintenance letter of credit, but no construction cost, donated fair value, municipal maintenance cost, wastewater volume, or selected-building allocation. No public-cost amount is inferred.

source.title: Council Bluffs City Council study-session packet — dedication of Google sewer improvements
source.notes: Google's letter states that the 2009 development agreement required Gable and Questa, at developer cost, to design and install an offsite sanitary sewer line, pump station, and appurtenances serving the 975-acre tract, and that the completed improvements were being dedicated to the City. No cost or fair value is stated.

research_updates.title: Local incentive audit found an unquantified franchise-fee and abatement reconciliation
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: City Council resolutions, development-agreement packets, official statements, principal-taxpayer tables, and agreement amendments for 2009-2021. Resolution 21-364 confirms that a 2011 franchise-fee cap modification was implemented late and that the second amendment adjusted the abatement schedule to resolve the inequity. The public resolution supplies no cap, repayment, credit, abatement percentage, foregone-revenue amount, cash transfer, or same-period service cost; it cannot support net fiscal or break-even calculations.

source.title: Council Bluffs Resolution 21-364
source.notes: The resolution authorizes a second amendment to the 2009 Gable/Questa development agreement. It says the 2011 amendment changed a franchise-fee cap, the change was not implemented until the current fiscal year, and the second amendment would adjust the abatement schedule to address the inequity. It provides no dollar amount.

research_updates.title: IEDA contract, amendment, compliance, and certification audit preserved identifier discrepancies
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: IEDA annual reports by status and county, Board packets, prior-award tables, and exact web queries for 08-HQJC-030, 12-HQJP-051, 23-HQJPTC-005, 23-HQJP-004, and 12-HQJP-071 covering 2007-2026. Completed-award quantities and the performing award are recorded. The March 2024 packet's two variant contract numbers are preserved as a source discrepancy rather than new awards. No public amendment text for the IEDA contracts, tax-credit certificate, claim/use schedule, recapture, repayment, or certified final benefit was found.

source.title: IEDA March 2024 board packet — Google prior awards
source.notes: The Cedar Rapids project review lists two Council Bluffs prior awards with the same dates, values, jobs, wages, and statuses used elsewhere, but renders their contract numbers as 23-HQJP-004 and 12-HQJP-071. The annual reports render them as 23-HQJPTC-005 and 12-HQJP-051; the identifier discrepancy is preserved and not treated as a new award.

research_updates.title: Iowa revenue audit found program rules but no project-specific exemption amount
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Iowa Department of Revenue data-center guidance, Iowa Code 423.3(95) references, registration form 78-013, annual-report form 78-014, and state tax-expenditure/incentive searches covering 2007-2026. The Department states that individual annual reports are confidential. No Google-specific exempt purchase base, sales/use-tax exemption, refund, electricity exemption, backup-fuel amount, certification, or local distribution was public, so no realized state or local fiscal cost is recorded.

source.title: Data Center Sales and Use Tax Incentives
source.notes: The guidance identifies Iowa Code 423.3(95), qualifying data-center purchases, registration form 78-013, and annual-report form 78-014. It states that individual annual reports are confidential; it does not disclose Google purchases, exemptions, refunds, electricity, fuel, or tax value.

research_updates.title: Water and sewer audit found a location total but no defensible building allocation
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Council Bluffs Water Works annual reports for 2006-2024 and board-report archive, City wastewater and planning pages, Iowa DNR Facility Explorer record 311068556, and Google environmental reports. CBWW ranks Google first and Tetra sixth among 2022 customers without customer quantities; DNR lists only general stormwater coverage. Google reports 2024 Council Bluffs location withdrawal, discharge, and consumption, but not campus, meter, building, potable/reclaimed, peak, cooling-cycle, rate, bill, or wastewater-load detail. The prior 25%/50%/75% selected-building allocation was removed; only an unallocated location identity remains modeled.

source.title: Google 2025 Environmental Report
source.notes: The location schedule reports 2024 Council Bluffs withdrawal of 1,410.3 million gallons, discharge of 400.1 million gallons, and consumption of 1,010.2 million gallons. The report does not allocate either Council Bluffs campus or a selected building, and discharge may be engineering-estimated where actual data is unavailable.

research_updates.title: Electric-utility audit confirmed MidAmerican service context but no facility load
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Iowa Utilities Board/Iowa Utilities Commission docket materials, MidAmerican resource-plan and tariff searches, Google energy disclosures, and legislative filings from 2012-2026. Record IDs included SPU-2021-0003 and Google's 2014 MidAmerican Wind VIII energy/REC arrangement. No Council Bluffs meter, annual kWh, peak MW, rate schedule, bill, interconnection capacity, upgrade cost, renewable-energy volume, or cost allocation was public. No electricity quantity is modeled.

source.title: Iowa Utilities Board FAQ — MidAmerican docket SPU-2021-0003
source.notes: The resource-planning docket identifies Google LLC among the participating technology companies and documents disputes over confidential MidAmerican filings. The public FAQ does not identify Council Bluffs load, usage, rate, interconnection capacity, infrastructure cost, or cost allocation.

research_updates.title: Workforce audit confirmed active recruiting but not establishment headcount
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Google Careers Council Bluffs location results, city principal-employer tables, IEDA job-compliance tables, and Google/Deloitte workforce disclosures. Current searches returned site lead, facilities technician, engineering, logistics, networking, operations, and program roles. The live posting confirms one opening and a national role pay band, not jobs filled or Council Bluffs payroll. No current establishment headcount, contractor count, annual-average FTE, resident-worker share, occupation distribution, or local payroll was public; the 60- and 70-job completed-award observations and the separate 31-job performing commitment remain the quantitative anchors.

source.title: Site Lead, Data Center Operations, Facilities Management — Council Bluffs
source.notes: The live Council Bluffs posting confirms ongoing facilities-management recruitment and lists a national pay range for one role. A careers search also returned Council Bluffs technician, engineering, logistics, networking, operations, and program roles, but neither the posting nor search results report site headcount, filled vacancies, local payroll, worker residence, or contractor employment.

research_updates.title: Recipient audit added a nonoverlapping $100,000 education grant
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Council Bluffs Community School District pages, Iowa Western publications, United Way of the Midlands disclosures, and Google community-impact materials for 2009-2024. Iowa Western directly reports its 2011 $100,000 grant, and Google's impact study separately reports approximately $285,000 to the school district during 2019-2023. A 2019 regional flood-relief disclosure combines Google.org, employee, and Council Bluffs data-center support across Iowa and Nebraska, so its $125,000 is not allocated here. No complete annual grant ledger or overlap reconciliation was public.

source.title: Iowa Western Alumni Magazine, Spring 2012
source.notes: The recipient reports that its Council Bluffs Enterprise Computing Center opened in 2011 and was developed with a $100,000 Google Tides Foundation grant.

research_updates.title: Later operator investment announcements remain outside the project ledger when geography is mixed
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Google Iowa location pages, operator announcements, Google/Deloitte impact studies, IEDA award tables, and city permit/assessment records spanning 2007-2026. Google's $7 billion two-year announcement combines Council Bluffs expansion, Cedar Rapids development, and statewide workforce support; the current Iowa page's cumulative total also spans multiple sites and vintages. Neither is entered as a Council Bluffs or selected-building forecast. Completed IEDA award costs remain separate and are not summed without overlap reconciliation.

source.title: How Google is driving a new era of American innovation in Iowa
source.notes: Google announced $7 billion of Iowa investment over two years spanning both Council Bluffs expansion and a new Cedar Rapids campus, plus a statewide electrical-workforce initiative. No Council Bluffs or building allocation is disclosed, so the amount is not entered as a project forecast.

project_description: Google Council Bluffs is a multi-building hyperscale data-center operation in Council Bluffs, Pottawattamie County, Iowa. The project key is one mapped inventory building, while the public record spans the broader Council Bluffs campuses, multiple operating parcels, completed 2007 and 2012 state-award projects, and a separate 2022 expansion still in performance; those scopes are not collapsed to the selected building. Documented development includes later electrical and cooling work, location-level water reporting, parcel-tax histories, and education grants.
